feature: Python support: grade, evidence and test runner
description: hexa parses Python imports and exports, grades Python projects, counts pytest and unittest output, refuses a grade over zero parsed files, and runs a single Python test by a built-in runner.

specs.description: A .py or .pyi path is Python.
specs.given: the paths `pkg/ports/repo.py` and `pkg/ports/repo.pyi`
specs.then: each returns `Language::Python`, in both `hexa-analysis` and `hexa-graph`

specs.description: Near-miss extensions are not Python.
specs.given: the paths `notes.pyc`, `script.py.bak`, `pyproject.toml` and `README.py.md`
specs.then: none returns `Language::Python`

specs.description: No crate other than the two analysis crates names the Python grammar.
specs.given: the workspace's Cargo.toml files
specs.then: `tree-sitter-python` appears only in `hexa-analysis` and `hexa-graph`; any other crate naming it fails the check

specs.description: Extension decides the Python language.
specs.given: any path
specs.then: the result is `Language::Python` exactly when the path ends in `.py` or `.pyi`, and the TypeScript, Go and Rust results are unchanged for every other path

specs.description: Absolute, from- and relative imports resolve to project files.
specs.given: a project with `nautobot_ssot/__init__.py`, `nautobot_ssot/ports.py` and `nautobot_ssot/usecases/sync.py`, where `sync.py` holds `import nautobot_ssot.ports` and `from ..ports import Repo`
specs.then: both are `ImportStatement`s whose `resolved_path` is `nautobot_ssot/ports.py`, and each is an import edge

specs.description: `from a import b` prefers the submodule, else the package.
specs.given: project A has `a/__init__.py` and `a/b.py`; project B has only `a/__init__.py`, which defines `b`
specs.when: `from a import b` is resolved in each project
specs.then: it resolves to `a/b.py` in A and to `a/__init__.py` in B

specs.description: A package under src/ resolves.
specs.given: a project with `src/app/__init__.py` and `src/app/domain.py`, and a file importing `from app.domain import Order`
specs.then: its `resolved_path` is `src/app/domain.py`

specs.description: An import under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` is an edge.
specs.given: `app/domain/order.py` holds `if TYPE_CHECKING:` followed by `from app.adapters.db import Session`, and `app/adapters/db.py` exists
specs.when: the project is analyzed with `app/domain` as domain and `app/adapters` as a secondary adapter
specs.then: the import is an edge from domain to adapters and is reported as a boundary violation

specs.description: Stdlib and third-party imports are neither edges nor violations.
specs.given: a domain file holding `import os`, `from django.db import models` and `import requests`, none of which is a project file
specs.then: none of the three is an import edge, and none is reported as a violation

specs.description: An edge exists exactly when the import names a project file.
specs.given: any Python import statement in any project
specs.then: it is an edge if and only if its `resolved_path` is an existing project file of the form `<module path>.py` or `<module path>/__init__.py` under the project root or a package root; an unresolved import is never a violation

specs.description: Without `__all__`, public top-level names are exports.
specs.given: a module with `def load()`, `class Repo`, `LIMIT = 5`, `def _helper()` and `_cache = {}` at top level, and a nested `def inner()` inside `load`
specs.then: the exports are exactly `load`, `Repo` and `LIMIT`

specs.description: `__all__` defines the exports.
specs.given: a module assigning `__all__ = ["Repo"]` and also defining public `def load()`
specs.then: the only export is `Repo`

specs.description: A name re-exported through `__init__.py` is not dead.
specs.given: `pkg/x.py` defines `y`, `pkg/__init__.py` holds `from .x import y`, and no other file imports `y`
specs.then: `y` in `pkg/x.py` is not reported as a dead export

specs.description: Private and nested names are never exports.
specs.given: a module whose only top-level names start with `_`, and which assigns no `__all__`
specs.then: there are no exports and no dead export is reported for it

specs.description: The export set is `__all__` or the public top-level names.
specs.given: any Python module
specs.then: they equal the names in `__all__` when the module assigns one, and otherwise the top-level `def`, `class` and assignment names not starting with `_`; dead-export detection applies the same rule it applies to TypeScript, Go and Rust

specs.description: A Django project with a tooling-only package.json is read as Python.
specs.given: a repository with `manage.py`, `pyproject.toml`, a package directory at the root holding `__init__.py` and Python files, and a `package.json` that is the only JavaScript tooling
specs.then: it names the language `python`, parses the package's `.py` files, does not report the language as TypeScript, and does not print the 'unsupported' line

specs.description: Several languages are all named and graded.
specs.given: a repository with `pyproject.toml` and Python sources, and `package.json` with TypeScript sources
specs.then: it names both `python` and `typescript`, and each language's files are graded

specs.description: Python files outside the convention need a declared layer.
specs.given: a package with `models.py`, `jobs.py` and `views.py` and no `analyze.layers` entry for them
specs.then: the three files are listed as unclassified and the grade is capped below A+; with `analyze.layers` entries for them, they are classified

specs.description: Excluded directories and test code are not graded as layers.
specs.given: a project with Python files under `migrations/`, `.venv/`, `venv/`, `site-packages/`, `node_modules/`, `__pycache__/`, `tests/`, and a file `pkg/test_sync.py`
specs.then: none of those files is counted in the layer coverage or reported as unclassified, and none adds an edge, dead export or violation

specs.description: The language is not chosen by manifest order alone.
specs.given: a repository with both `requirements.txt` and `package.json`, and Python sources only
specs.then: the language is not reported as TypeScript only, and the Python files are graded

specs.description: Every detected language is graded and the layer scan covers package directories.
specs.given: any repository
specs.then: every language whose manifest and sources are present is named and its files graded; for Python, the layer scan covers every package directory, not only `src/`, and never the default-excluded directories

specs.description: pytest's summary is counted.
specs.given: exit status 0 and output `== 5 passed in 0.12s ==`, and separately `5 passed in 0.12s` (the `-q` form)
specs.then: each is `Evidence::Passed { tests: 5 }`

specs.description: A pytest failure line fails.
specs.given: exit status 0 and output `== 3 failed, 5 passed, 1 skipped in 0.31s ==`
specs.then: the result is `Evidence::Failed` naming 3 failed tests

specs.description: Zero-test and skip-only pytest runs are vacuous.
specs.given: exit status 0 and output, in turn, `no tests ran in 0.01s`, `collected 0 items`, `== 4 skipped in 0.02s ==`, and `== 2 xfailed in 0.02s ==`
specs.then: each is `Evidence::Vacuous`, never `Passed` and never `Unrecognised`

specs.description: `KNOWN_RUNNERS` names the new runners.
specs.given: the constant `KNOWN_RUNNERS`
specs.then: it names both pytest and unittest; a value naming neither fails

specs.description: A pytest summary passes only with passed tests and no failures.
specs.given: any pytest summary with counts p passed, f failed, s skipped and x xfailed, and exit status 0
specs.then: the result is `Failed` when f > 0, otherwise `Passed { tests: p }` when p > 0, otherwise `Vacuous`; skipped and xfailed never add to the passed count

specs.description: Zero parsed files is 'not graded'.
specs.given: a directory with no source file hexa parses
specs.then: it prints "not graded" and prints no letter grade and no score out of 100

specs.description: An empty grade never exits green under a gate.
specs.given: a directory in which hexa parses zero files
specs.when: `hexa analyze . --exit-code`, and separately `hexa analyze . --grade A`, run
specs.then: each exits non-zero; printing A+ 100/100 with exit 0 is the refused outcome

specs.description: No letter without parsed files, in any language.
specs.given: any project, in any language or none
specs.then: the output contains no letter grade, says "not graded", and `--exit-code` and `--grade` both exit non-zero

specs.description: unittest's OK counts the run minus the skipped.
specs.given: exit status 0 and output `Ran 40 tests in 1.2s` followed by `OK (skipped=33)`
specs.then: the result is `Evidence::Passed { tests: 7 }`

specs.description: A plain unittest OK counts every test.
specs.given: exit status 0 and output `Ran 5 tests in 0.002s` followed by `OK`
specs.then: the result is `Evidence::Passed { tests: 5 }`

specs.description: A framework wrapper is read by its output.
specs.given: a gate `nautobot-server test` (or `invoke unittest`) that exits 0 and prints `Ran 12 tests in 3.4s` followed by `OK`
specs.then: the result is `Evidence::Passed { tests: 12 }`, read from the output and not from the command name

specs.description: Failures, errors and zero-test runs do not pass.
specs.given: exit status 0 and output, in turn, `Ran 5 tests` followed by `FAILED (failures=1, errors=2)`, then `Ran 0 tests in 0.000s` followed by `OK`, then `Ran 3 tests` followed by `OK (skipped=3)`
specs.then: the first is `Evidence::Failed`, and the second and third are `Evidence::Vacuous`

specs.description: The unittest count is N minus skipped.
specs.given: any unittest output `Ran N tests` followed by `OK` or `OK (skipped=k)` with k ≤ N, and exit status 0
specs.then: the result is `Passed { tests: N − k }` when N − k > 0 and `Vacuous` otherwise; any `FAILED (...)` line makes it `Failed` whatever N is

specs.description: `py` has a built-in pytest runner.
specs.given: no `test.runners.py` entry, and the reference `pkg/tests/test_sync.py::test_one` with a `pyproject.toml` in `pkg/`
specs.when: `runner_for("py", {})` is called and the test is run
specs.then: a Python runner is returned, and it runs `python3 -m pytest pkg/tests/test_sync.py::test_one -q` (with the file path as seen from that directory) from `pkg/`, the nearest directory at or above the file holding `pyproject.toml`, `pytest.ini`, `tox.ini` or `setup.cfg`

specs.description: Python test files are recognised for sealing.
specs.given: the paths `app/tests/models.py`, `app/test_sync.py` and `app/sync_test.py`
specs.then: each returns true

specs.description: A configured runner wins over the built-in.
specs.given: `test.runners.py` is set to `nautobot-server test {name}`
specs.then: it returns `Runner::Configured` with that template, not the built-in Python runner

specs.description: Zero or several tests do not pass a single-test run.
specs.given: a built-in Python test run whose output reports `no tests ran`, and another reporting `3 passed`
specs.then: the first is `Vacuous` and the second `Ambiguous(3)`; neither is `Passed`

specs.description: Ordinary Python modules are not test files.
specs.given: the paths `app/models.py`, `app/contest.py` and `app/testing_utils.py`
specs.then: each returns false

specs.description: A Python test passes only when exactly one test ran and passed.
specs.given: any run of the built-in Python runner
specs.then: it is `Passed` if and only if the output reports exactly one test that ran and passed and none failed; zero is `Vacuous`, more than one is `Ambiguous`

specs.description: The out-of-scope items are named as not done.
specs.given: this ADR marked built
specs.when: its Built line and status are read
specs.then: generating Python tests by `hexa spec tests` and `hexa spec red`, Python output from `hexa scaffold` and `hexa init --scaffold`, and `hexa init` explaining that `lifecycle_enforcement` defaults to "mandatory" are each listed as outside this ADR, with a separate ADR or gap for each

specs.description: This ADR is not cited as having delivered the out-of-scope items.
specs.given: a change log, Built line or gap closure that cites ADR-2611211324 as delivering Python test generation, Python scaffolding, or the `hexa init` lifecycle message
specs.when: it is reviewed against this ADR
specs.then: the claim is refused; those items remain open until their own ADR or gap closes them

specs.description: The Python example is graded.
specs.given: `examples/stress/game-wordle-py`
specs.then: it reports a letter grade of A+, or a grade whose violations are exactly the planted ones, and the example's README says so

specs.description: The two target repositories are measured and recorded.
specs.given: `netbox-plugin` and `nautobot-ssot-plugin`
specs.when: `hexa analyze` runs on each and this ADR is marked built
specs.then: the Built line records, for each repository, its grade, the number of files with a layer, and the `analyze.layers` entries it needed

specs.description: This ADR is not built while the README or Built line is unchanged.
specs.given: the game-wordle-py README still calls it "a tree it cannot read", or the Built line lacks either target repository's grade, layered-file count or `analyze.layers`
specs.when: this ADR is checked as built
specs.then: it is not built

specs.description: hexa's own grade is unchanged.
specs.given: the hexa repository after the change
specs.then: it stays A+ 100/100; any lower result fails the final phase

amendments.by: Claude (agent, in craigjohnson's session; for review)
amendments.reason: S05 asserted two violations for two import lines of one module from one file; the grade counts one edge per target (one_edge_per_target: one crossing costs ten points once), so the fixture now checks each import form alone. The scenario is unchanged: both forms resolve to nautobot_ssot/ports.py and each is an edge.
